Getting started with FlightLens

Vishal Sampath

getting-started.Rmd

Purpose

FlightLens helps a junior aviation analyst investigate historical operations. Its question is: for a selected NYC route and months in 2013, how did recorded departure-delay rates differ by airline or scheduled departure period?

Install and launch

Install FlightLens from the project repository and launch the app. The application uses data included in the installed package, without downloading records at runtime.

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-issvish")
flightlens::launch_app()

Use the app

Start with JFK to LAX and all months, then select June through August. Switch from airlines to scheduled departure periods to investigate whether the comparison changes.

  • Departure airport: the NYC origin code.
  • Destination: the destination airport code.
  • Month range: inclusive months; 1 is January, 12 is December.
  • Compare: airlines or scheduled local departure periods.
  • Delay threshold: minutes at or above which a recorded departure is counted as delayed.
  • Minimum observed count: hides groups with fewer recorded departure delays.

Periods are night 00-05, morning 06-11, afternoon 12-17 and evening 18-23. They use scheduled departure hours, not actual departure hours.

Read the outputs

The bar chart shows the percentage of recorded delays meeting the threshold. A 15-minute threshold includes a flight delayed exactly 15 minutes.

Delayed percentage=100×observed delays at or above the thresholdall observed departure delays. \text{Delayed percentage} =100\times\frac{\text{observed delays at or above the threshold}} {\text{all observed departure delays}}.

The coverage text counts all selected records, observed delays and missing delays before groups are hidden. The table shows the counts for each displayed group. Therefore, its counts may not sum to the coverage text when groups are excluded.

The mean and median are measured in minutes. Missing percentages use all group records, while delayed percentages use only observed delays.

Reproduce a route comparison 

summer_route <- filter_flights(
  flight_data, origin = "JFK", destination = "LAX", months = 6:8
)
airline_summary <- summarise_delays(
  summer_route, group = "airline", threshold = 15
)
eligible <- airline_summary[airline_summary$n_observed >= 30, ]
knitr::kable(eligible, digits = 1)
group n_total n_observed n_missing missing_pct n_delayed delayed_pct mean_delay median_delay
American Airlines Inc. 810 808 2 0.2 157 19.4 12.3 -2
Delta Air Lines Inc. 611 611 0 0.0 142 23.2 11.9 0
JetBlue Airways 495 495 0 0.0 152 30.7 16.7 1
United Air Lines Inc. 519 517 2 0.4 100 19.3 10.4 -1
Virgin America 457 456 1 0.2 107 23.5 18.5 1

Among the displayed groups for this route and period, United Air Lines Inc. had the lowest recorded delayed percentage, 19.3%, using the 15-minute threshold. This describes these observations rather than proving one airline performs better under identical operating conditions.

Compare departure periods 

period_summary <- summarise_delays(
  summer_route, group = "period", threshold = 15
)
knitr::kable(period_summary, digits = 1)
group n_total n_observed n_missing missing_pct n_delayed delayed_pct mean_delay median_delay
Afternoon (12-17) 1155 1151 4 0.3 278 24.2 14.3 0
Evening (18-23) 677 677 0 0.0 300 44.3 31.0 9
Morning (06-11) 1060 1059 1 0.1 80 7.6 1.8 -2

Compare the observed sample sizes and missingness before comparing percentages. These period groups combine airlines and are not controlled estimates of time-of-day effects.

Test a stricter delay definition 

stricter <- summarise_delays(
  summer_route, group = "airline", threshold = 60
)
comparison <- data.frame(
  airline = airline_summary$group,
  delayed_15_pct = airline_summary$delayed_pct,
  delayed_60_pct = stricter$delayed_pct
)
knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 1)
airline delayed_15_pct delayed_60_pct
American Airlines Inc. 19.4 9.3
Delta Air Lines Inc. 23.2 5.9
JetBlue Airways 30.7 10.7
United Air Lines Inc. 19.3 6.6
Virgin America 23.5 8.1

For a fixed group and observed sample, the 60-minute percentage cannot exceed the 15-minute percentage. Airline rankings can still change, which is why changing the threshold is a meaningful interaction.

Empty and weak states 

empty <- filter_flights(flight_data, origin = character())
nrow(empty)
#> [1] 0
summarise_delays(empty)
#> [1] group        n_total      n_observed   n_missing    missing_pct 
#> [6] n_delayed    delayed_pct  mean_delay   median_delay
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

In the app, selecting a route without records produces guidance to change the airports or months. Setting the minimum to 1,000,000 produces a message to lower it. Zero or a blank minimum produces an input-validation message.

Groups with few observed delays can have unstable percentages. The display minimum is not a statistical test, and a single remaining group cannot support a between-group comparison.

Data and limitations

The public source is nycflights13 version 1.0.2, which distributes the data under CC0 (dataset documentation).

The flight data reference attributes the original records to RITA, Bureau of Transportation Statistics, and defines negative delay values as early departures (field definitions).

The preparation script retains all rows and missing departure delays. Missing values are not interpreted as on-time departures or confirmed cancellations.

These are 2013 observations, not current travel recommendations. Differences may reflect schedules, weather, airline mix and other operating conditions. No causal adjustment or confidence intervals are provided.
